name: Utad Centro Universitario de Tecnologia y Arte Digital
overview:
IMPORTANT - ADDITIONAL PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS

Students must demonstrate a B2 level in Spanish via an interview with a Spanish speaker (organized by IAFF team)



Camilo José Cela University is a private establishment created in the 2000s.


The campus covers 100,000 square meters, is 15 minutes from Madrid, and offers a friendly place suitable for working in small groups.


U-Tad is a benchmark university center in the training of future leaders of the digital world, and has a student population of nearly 1,300 students.


U-Tad takes a practical approach with real projects, working with the same technology as leading companies and welcoming professionals and entrepreneurs with international success to the campus.


U-Tad collaborates with companies like Amazon, Autodesk, Adobe, Microsoft, or HP, as well as the animation studios Ilion.


Also, companies such as Banco Santander, Orange, Phone House, BI Geek Software, Altran, OpenSystems, PWC, among others, entrust the training of their employees to U-Tad in the field of data engineering.


The U-Tad campus is located in Las Rozas (1 hour from Madrid).


Classes are taught in Spanish, and the university recommends a minimum level of B1.


No official test is required, however, you must take an interview in Spanish with the international relations office in order to put this university as one of your choices.


The interviews will take place in December, prior to the international jury.


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on this country, here.
administrative:
1) Application Dossier


Once the IAFF office has sent your nomination, the partner university will contact you directly by email to start your application.

All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the EMEA Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.

To be completed with your Epitech bachelor campus administration during the registration period for Tech4 (usually in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2) Visa


  • For European students, a valid passport or national ID card is sufficient to travel to Europe (exception: the UK).
  • For non-European students or students with a non-European citizenship, please check the immigration office of the host country to check the visa process and fees.
  • Students in France can use this website:
  • https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/


3) Insurance


For European students


The European Health Insurance Card (CEAM) is nominative and individual. This card certifies your rights to Health Insurance in Europe.


To obtain your card, log in to your Ameli account at least two months before your departure.


It is free of charge and will be sent to your place within two weeks. You can also download it online.


More information: https://www.ameli.fr/assure/droits-demarches/europe-international/protection-sociale-etranger/etudes-etranger


For non-European students:


You must register for a private health insurance to cover your full stay.


Please check with your parents, bank, or any private insurance company for more information depending on the desired coverage.


Please register via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ariane) platform to be aware of any news (terrorist attack, tsunami, earthquake…) in your host country — for French citizens only: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html
accomodation:
It is advisable to start well ahead of time in your search for accommodations in Madrid, but be aware that the campus is 1 hour away by public transport. If you wish, you can also search for accommodations located in Las Rozas (location of campus).


For help in finding an apartment, you can explore the following sites:

https://www.vibbo.com/pisos-y-casas/

https://www.pisocompartido.com/

https://www.idealista.com/
